claim: Prompt-based self-reported confidence in LLM agents systematically overestimates task success rate (overconfidence), and this bias is structural—attributed to the agent's incentive to justify committed actions rather than critique them—rather than method-specific.
falsifier: On a new LLM agent and task, elicit prompt-based confidence after action commitment and compare reliability diagram; test whether overconfidence persists under different commitment levels or when confidence is elicited before action.

conditions: Observed across every method (ReAct+UE, UAM, proposed decomposition) and every benchmark (WebShop, ALFWorld, REAL, clarification variants)
All reliability curves lie below the diagonal
Interpreted as structural bias of prompt-based self-reported confidence due to commitment justification
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported LLM backbones, benchmarks, and prompt-based confidence methods; transfer to other confidence elicitation paradigms (e.g., logprob-based, multi-sample) is unestablished.

claim: Self-evolution of experiment strategies through persistent memory and multi-agent learning increases the execution success rate of automated experiments across multiple stages.
falsifier: Implement a multi-agent system with self-evolution of experiment strategies using persistent memory, and measure execution success rates before and after evolution across similar experiment stages.

conditions: The system includes an engineer agent responsible for experiment implementation and execution
The system uses an experimentation memory that captures effective strategies from code search trajectories and best-performing implementations
The evolution manager agent distills insights from prior agent interactions into reusable knowledge
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported EvoScientist system, its specific agent architecture, and the evaluated experiment stages; transfer beyond these conditions is unestablished.

title: Self-evolution of experiment strategies for mean execution success rate
